chunks: Muhammad ibn Aqeel from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Yazeed Al-Rifa'i, raising it (to the Imam).

That the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was asked about the standing at the Mountain (Jabal al-Rahmah), why it was not in the Sanctuary (Haram)? So he said: 'Because the Ka'bah is His House and the Haram is its door. So when they came to it as delegates, He stopped them at the door, supplicating.'

It was said to him: 'So why has Al-Mashar Al-Haram become inside the Haram?' He said: 'Because when He permitted them to enter, He stopped them at the second Veil. So when their supplication at it was prolonged, He permitted them to offer their sacrifice. So when they fulfilled their minor rituals, they were purified by it from the sins which were a veil between them and Him. He permitted them the visitation upon purity.'

It was said to him: 'So why was fasting prohibited during the Days of Tashreeq?' He said: 'Because the people are visitors of Allah, and they are in His hospitality, and it is not fitting for a Host that He should make His guests fast.'

It was said to him: 'So what is the meaning of hanging onto the curtains of the Ka'bah?' He said: 'It is like a man who has a felony and a sin with another, so he hangs onto his garment, supplicating to him and humbling himself to him that he would overlook his sin.'

key_terms.أَيَّامُ التَّشْرِيقِ: The Days of Tashreeq (11th, 12th, 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.الْمَشْعَرُ الْحَرَامُ: Al-Mashar Al-Haram (the sacred site at Muzdalifah)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and legal reasoning behind the Hajj rituals and the prohibition of fasting during Tashreeq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elucidates the metaphysical wisdom behind Hajj rituals, framing the pilgrim's journey as a progression from the 'door' (Arafat) to the 'curtain' (Muzdalifah) and finally into the divine presence. It interprets the prohibition of fasting during Tashreeq as an act of divine hospitality, where God, as the host, does not weary His guests, while the act of touching the Ka'bah's curtains symbolizes a sinner's humble supplication for pardon. This narrative reinforces the Shia emphasis on the spiritual dimensions of ritual acts (ma'ani) alongside their legal forms (ahkam).

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Aqeel Bin Al Hassan Bin Al Husayn, from Ali Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hassan, from Muhammad Bin Yazeed Al Rafa’iy,

(It has been narrated) raising it that Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the pausing by the mountain, how come it did not happen to be in ‘الْحَرَمِ’ the Sanctuary? So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Because the Kabah is His<sup>azwj</sup> House and the الْحَرَمِ is its door. So when the delegations come over, He<sup>azwj</sup> Pauses them by the door, supplicating’.

It was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So why have the Signs of ‘الْحَرَمِ’ (Al-Harram) the Sanctuary) come to be inside the Al-Harram?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Because when Permission was Granted to them with the entry, they were Paused by the second Veil. So when their supplication were prolonged at it, Permission was Granted to them with the offering of the sacrifice. So when they fulfilled their rituals, they were purified by it from the sins which were an obstacle between them and Him<sup>azwj</sup>, He<sup>azwj</sup> Permitted them with the visitation upon the purity’.

It was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So why are the Fasts Prohibited during the days of Al-Tashreek (11<sup>th</sup>, 12<sup>th</sup>, and 13<sup>th</sup> of Zilhajj)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Because the people are visitors of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and they are among His<sup>azwj</sup> guests, and it is not Commendable for the Host that He<sup>azwj</sup> would Make His<sup>azwj</sup> guests to Fast’.

It was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So the attachment with the curtains of the Kabah, for which meaning is it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Like a man who has a felony with another and a sin, so he hangs on to his clothes, beseeching to him, and humbling himself to him that he would overlook from his sins’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn ‘Aqil has narrated from al-Hassan ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hassan from Muhammad ibn Yazid aI-Rifa’ ‘iy who in a marfu‘ manner has narrated from ’Amir al-Mu’minin the following: “

’Amir al-Mu’minin was asked about staying on the hill, why it is not inside the Sacred area (al- Haram)?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘It is because al-Ka‘bah is His house and al-Haram (the sacred area) is its door. When people wanted to come to His House, He made them stand, wait at the door and appeal for permission.’

It was asked from him, ‘Why is al-Mash‘ar al-Haram part of al-Haram?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘It is because when permission was given to come, He made them to stop on the second barrier but when their pleading prolonged, permission was granted to them to move their offerings closer. When they cleaned themselves with it, they became clean of sins, which were as barriers between them, and He granted permission to visit (His House) in a clean condition.’

It was then asked, ‘Why is fasting during the bright days not permissible?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘It is because people are Allah’s visitors, they are His guests and it is not nice for a host that his guests remain fasting.’

He was asked, ‘Why should one hold to the curtains of al-Ka‘bah and what does it mean?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘It is like one who has committed a crime against another person; thus he holds to his clothes and expresses humility before him to forgive him his sins and crime.’”
